- Goal: Validate LLM assist for discharge summaries (accuracy + hallucination checks) across 10k historical notes.  
- Primary success metrics: Factual correctness (binary per-item), hallucination rate (tokens), and ROUGE-L for extraction fields.  
- Constraints: PHI-sensitive; data will be on a private S3 bucket, we need instructions for secure upload to Redwood Private.  

Can you share:  
1) Preferred dataset CSV/JSONL schema for Redwood eval runner (we have mixed note formats)  
2) Suggested model(s) to test first (cost/latency tradeoffs)  
3) Prompt set you recommend we start with (we can tweak)  
4) Rough timeline and scoring window (how long does Redwood need to run the 10k items?)

Liam — great to chat, thanks for the clear goals. High level answers and next steps below; I attached our quickstart PDF and a starter prompt_set_v1.jsonl you can drop into the eval runner.

1) Dataset schema (preferred): JSONL where each line is a JSON object with keys: id, patient_id (hashed), note_text, reference_summary, labels (array of ground-truth extractions), metadata {encounter_date, note_type}. If CSV is easier, use these columns with note_text quoted. We included a small example in the attached carelink_eval_dataset.csv.  

2) Recommended models to start (order matters):  
   - Llama-3-8B-q4: low-cost baseline, good extraction precision when prompted for fielded output.
   - Redwood-7B-fp16: best balance of latency and factuality in our benchmarks for clinical notes.
   - Redwood-xl-13B-quant: higher-quality reference run if you want the upper-bound on accuracy (we run this as an optional compare).

3) Prompt set: prompt_set_v1.jsonl includes 6 prompts: short instruction, extraction template, hallucination probe, confidence calibration, red-team phrasing to catch omission, and boundary-case examples. Start with v1; we'll iterate after the 200-sample run.

4) Timeline & compute: For 10k items we expect ~6–10 hours on a standard dedicated pool for the 8B runs with default batching. The 13B pass as a reference will add ~3–4 hours. If you need a faster turnaround we can schedule parallel workers (extra cost).

Security notes: For Private deployments we require S3 presigned-POST instructions or direct access via a temporary role. We'll send the secure upload instructions in a separate message (I copied Ben + Karthik who'll own the onboarding steps and scoring rubric).

Next steps (ask list):

- Ben/Karthik: please confirm scoring rubric below and assign a scorer for clinical label validation.
- Hannah: schedule a 30-min scoring walkthrough after sample run to align thresholds.

Attaching: prompt_set_v1.jsonl, carelink_eval_dataset.csv, redwood-eval-runner-quickstart.pdf

Best — Hannah

Ben / Karthik — forwarding Liam's ask and my reply. High priority: we need a clear scoring rubric for the 200-sample pilot and resource assignment for clinical label reconciliation. My suggested rubric (quick draft):

Scoring rubric (pilot - binary + continuous):
- Factual correctness: binary per item (0/1) against reference_summary (1 = all requested facts present and correct).
- Field extraction accuracy: per-field F1 (precision/recall averaged across specified fields).
- Hallucination flag: number of hallucinated spans per output (annotator-marked).
- Confidence calibration: model confidence bucket vs. ground truth (calibration error).
- Regression guardrails: baseline check vs. historical Redwood run on the same sample (if available) — if factual correctness drops >4% compared to baseline, block promotion and trigger root-cause.

Operational asks:
- Ben: can your team provide a reviewer (clinical SME) for 3–4 hours to validate the 200-sample pilot? Preferably someone who can do quick binary checks + highlight hallucinated spans.
- Karthik: can you confirm runner config (batch size, quantization profile) and which model variants we should pin for the pilot? I recommend Llama-3-8B-q4 (default) and Redwood-7B-fp16 (comparison). If you think Redwood-xl-13B-quant is necessary for this pilot, flag cost estimate.
